submission.justification:
Radiator-R3 at 3 cm thickness is recommended as the optimal balance between performance and long-term reliability. This choice achieves 3.819 sigma pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c, which is the best performance for this radiator at any thickness tested (1-6 cm range).

While Radiator-R2 offers superior separation (4.656 sigma at 3 cm), its porous structure without hydrophobic treatment poses significant risk of failing the critical 10-year humidity ageing requirement (<10% transparency loss). Since the radiator cannot be replaced during the detector's operational lifetime, this risk is unacceptable.

Radiator-R3 was specifically engineered with hydrophobic treatment to address humidity concerns in porous radiators, making it the most reliable option for meeting the ageing requirement while still delivering strong particle identification performance. The 3 cm thickness optimizes the separation power for this radiator material.

Radiator-R1, while potentially most stable as a solid material, offers significantly lower separation (2.922 sigma), which would compromise the physics goals of the detector unnecessarily when R3 provides both good performance and adequate protection against ageing.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 at 3 cm achieves 3.819 sigma separation, which is the best performance for this radiator across all thicknesses. While Radiator-R2 offers higher separation (4.656 sigma), it likely fails the ageing requirement, making R3 the best viable option.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate radiators in the specifications document.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 features hydrophobic treatment specifically designed to resist humidity effects in porous radiators. While explicit ageing test data was not provided in the documents, the hydrophobic treatment indicates this radiator was engineered to meet ageing requirements, unlike untreated porous Radiator-R2.
The recommended thickness of 3 cm is within the specified range of 1-6 cm.
